newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah eases amid economic deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah eases amid economic deregulation.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah eased against the dollar in moderate late trading on Monday due to sufficient liquidity, with eyes seen on the government annoncement of the long-awaited economic deregulation package, dealers said.

"The deregulation package would in general have positive impact on the rupiah as we expect the economy to be more efficient, but for now the market is waiting for more details," one foreign bank dealer said.
Indonesia on Monday unveiled its latest economic deregulation package, cutting tariffs on 1,600 items.
The package includes a move to limit loans to property developers for land purchases, the central bank governor said.
Indonesia's last major economic reform package was in June last year when it cut import tariffs on 1,497 items, simplified trade procedures and offered incentives for export-oriented firms.
Spot rupiah was at 2,431.00/31.50 at 0955 GMT against an opening of 2,429.80/30.50.
Dealers said liquidity was slightly tight in early trading, but it eased later in the day.
They said the market was mostly liquidity driven, as market talk of a possible band widening seemed to wane for now.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,430.50/31.00 and 2,429.00/29.25, respectively.
Band widening was the focus last Thursday and Friday, with the central bank seen widening the band from its current eight percent.
Overnight swaps were at 0.50/0.55 points. Tom/next was at 0.42/0.45 points. One-month swaps were at 14.25/15.50, two at 26.5/28.0, three at 40.0/41.5 and six at 81.50/82.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,428/2,620 and the conversion band by one point to 2,428/2,476 on Monday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
